text:
rachel: Heads-up — noticing a lot of GPU node churn in ap-southeast this morning. Nodes are coming up, getting a few pods, then being vacuumed within ~8-12m. Cost spike on the infra dashboard. Anyone tracking?
dave: saw the alert, looks correlated with scale-to-zero kicks after short idle windows. autoscaler seems aggressive.
autoscaler-bot: [scale event] cluster: gpu-prod-ap-southeast | scaled down 12 -> 5 (reason: unneeded) | scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
nina: ugh. that 10m default is brutal for bursty workloads. our KV cache promotion + coldstart penalty means we pay latency and token-cost later. Can we try adding a "keep-warm" tier label and a longer shelf-life?
paul: +1. proposal: add a small standby nodepool with labeled nodes that the scheduler prefers for gpu workloads and set scale-down-unneeded-time=30m for that pool. We keep the regular pool aggressive.
rachel: curious on sequencing — do we change cluster-autoscaler args per nodepool or do we rely on separate nodegroup config?
nina: separate nodepool is cleaner. CA flags are cluster level, but GKE/ASG can have per-group settings (e.g., evictionPolicy, maxSurge style settings). For k8s CA we can fake it by keeping min-size=1 for standby and controlling target via autoscaler policies.
dave: here's a quick diff I tried locally:
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: ClusterAutoscalerConfig
metadata:
  name: gpu-standby
spec:
  scaleDownUnneededTime: 30m
  scaleDownUtilizationThreshold: 0.3
```
(not a direct k8s object in our cluster, but used my local wrapper to template CA args)
paul: also consider node-probe backoff jitter. If kubelet readiness probes are noisy during boot, CA counts nodes as low-util more often. We should bump node-probe-timeout from 5s -> 15s for gpu bootstrap.
rachel: cost side: ops dashboard shows churn tax ~ $4.2k last 24h in ap-southeast. If we keep 3 standby nodes all day it's ~ $600/day. Need to model tradeoff: latency regressions vs churn tax.
dave: spreadsheet quick numbers: coldstart latency + KV refill cost ~ 1.5s + extra GPU cycles; for customer traffic that matters for p99. For internal batch jobs maybe not. We should target keep-warm for production routes only.
ops-signal-bot: [metric] p99 latency for llm/generate in ap-southeast up 22% during churn windows
nina: ok experiment plan: 1) create gpu-standby nodepool with min=1, max=3, taint: keep-warm=true:NoSchedule 2) add nodeAffinity for production deployments to prefer keep-warm nodes 3) extend probe timeouts & scale-down-unneeded-time in templated CA 4) run for 48h and compare churn tax vs p99
paul: +1. add a short TTL on affinity so non-prod can still bin-pack if needed. e.g., nodeAffinity preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution with weight 50.
rachel: who can own rollout? dave? if we see reduced churn we can reduce cost elsewhere.
dave: I can own the rollout. I'll create the pool and a PR for chart values. Will also instrument a custom metric: node_churn_events{region} to track.
nina: can you also add a gate that flips based on cost delta? want to auto-revert if standby cost > churn savings after 24h.
dave: yep — will add a circuit in the runbook: revert if churn_tax_reduction < 10% after 24h.
paul: small nit — use spot/interruptible for standby? might kill the point. prefer on-demand to avoid preemption during the 48h test.
rachel: sounds good. dave assign to yourself and post PR link here. thanks all :thumbsup:
